Subject: Post-call: Production readiness & deployment playbook for HelixBio

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. I’ve summarized the pain, goals, and a tentative deployment playbook below.

Pain points we heard
- Current inference endpoints for on-prem model are spiky: 200–800 TPS bursts, 80% of requests under 100 tokens but tails up to 2k tokens.
- High P95 latency (400–600ms) during morning batch jobs — impacts UI features.
- Tight compliance: customer PII must not leave their VPC (will likely require Private deployment or strict routing).

Goals / success criteria
- P50 ≤ 80ms for short responses, P95 ≤ 250ms for common queries; support burst to 800 TPS with graceful degradation.
- Per-request cost target: keep >=2x cost improvement relative to current host (rough target we discussed).
- Ability to roll forward/back model versions with minimal downtime; audit logs for 90 days.

Suggested deployment playbook (high level)
1) Short term (Pilot) — Redwood Dedicated in us-west region with reserved capacity sized for steady-state 250 TPS + burst pool. Enable prefix KV caching for common prompts and 8-bit quantization for recent model weights.
2) Mid term (Compliance-ready) — Private deployment (VPC) in HelixBio account with Redwood control plane; HSM/KMS integration for key management. Keep canary rollout for model changes.
3) Long term — Autoscaling policies tested with replay dataset; add regional failover to us-east for DR.

Technical notes we’ll validate in next doc: model architecture (decoder-only Llama-family variant?), tokenization profile, peak token/sec estimates, and sustained GPU utilization.

Attachments included: latency-metrics.csv (sample traces), topology-diagram.png (initial sketch).

Next steps (owner / ETA)
- Helix: share representative replay traces + current token distribution (Alex) — ETA Thu 6/17
- Redwood: produce a sizing matrix (Marissa) — ETA Tue 6/22
- Technical deep-dive (Dev) to propose kernel/quantization options and Dedicated vs Private cost delta — schedule Wed 6/23

I’ve put a short agenda for the deep-dive in the Drive folder (link below). If we’re aligned I’ll share a short MLP (mutual action plan) after you send the traces.

Hi Alex / Priya —

I pulled together a short technical note based on today’s call and the telemetry you said you’d send. Key points and concrete recommendations below.

Observed / assumed workload (from call)
- Burst window: 200–800 TPS (peak sustained ~2–5 min), median request 60 tokens, tail requests up to 2k tokens.
- Model: decoder-only, ~13B parameters (approx), fp16 baseline.

Latency and throughput SLOs (recommendations)
- Target SLOs: P50 <= 80ms (short), P95 <= 250ms for <=200 token requests. For 2k token tails expect P95 > 1s; define SLAs with graceful degradation (token-limit truncation + early-exit).
- Batching: dynamic batching with upper limit per-GPU to avoid P95 spikes; target batch sizes 8–16 for short responses, adaptive to sequence length.
- KV cache: enable KV caching for repeated conversational prefixes; expect 15–30% cost reduction and lower tail latency for dialogs.

Serving & topology options
- Dedicated (recommended pilot): 4 x A100-equivalent nodes with a burst autoscaler (reserve capacity for 250 TPS steady + 2x burst pool). Continuous batching runtime avoids cold-starts for the common path.
- Private (compliance): identical runtime inside customer VPC; control plane in Redwood but data plane isolated. We’ll provide a deployment manifest and a bootstrap script.

Quantization & accuracy tradeoffs
- 8-bit (GPTQ-style) recommended for cost/throughput if you can tolerate minor top-k rerank differences on edge cases. We propose an eval sweep: 1) baseline fp16, 2) 8-bit quant, 3) 4-bit experimental — measure exact-match and downstream NLU metrics on your eval set.

Failure modes & fallbacks
- If GPU saturation occurs, automatic fallback to smaller model variant (lower-latency model) for non-critical routes and enqueue non-urgent requests to batch worker.
- Region/failover: cross-region routing with model variant policy to avoid cold cache penalties.

Action items I’ll deliver by Tue 6/22 (attachment: proposal-draft.pdf)
- Sizing matrix for Dedicated vs Private with expected P95 under target workloads.
- Quantization plan and evaluation script.
- Example autoscaling policy JSON and canary rollout plan.

Attachment: proposal-draft.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

If this looks right I’ll slot a 60-minute technical deep-dive tomorrow or Wed and bring a small replay harness to run a short stress test with your traces.
